company_name: PICC Property and Casualty Company Limited
model: P&C insurer FCFE at cost of equity, net debt held at zero (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 IFRS 17 insurance revenue (FY2025 AR consolidated income statement; CSV revenue column). Insurance revenue excludes investment income, which sits inside profit before tax and therefore inside ebitda_margin_path. H1 2026 insurance revenue 254,617 (+2.2%); original premium income 327,529 (+1.3%), market share 33.3%.
inputs.share_count_basis: 22,242,765,303 ordinary shares (domestic + H) unchanged since 2015 (CSV shares_outstanding 22,242 every period FY2018-H1 2026). No share option or incentive scheme, no convertibles, no buybacks: basic EPS = diluted EPS (RMB1.452 both, H1 2026 interim income statement). Domestic and H shares rank pari passu for dividends, so the per-share value is on the total count. Held FLAT.
inputs.net_debt_treatment: Held at ZERO, the insurers convention in this folder (1339.HK, 1336.HK, LGEN.L, PRU, GL). Bonds payable RMB12,246M at 30 June 2026 (12,076 at FY2025) are RMB12.0bn 10-year capital supplementary bonds issued November 2024 (H1 2026 interim report: Tier 2 regulatory capital); their coupon is in finance costs inside profit before tax, so the flows already pay for them. Securities sold under repurchase agreements are netted inside total investment income (interest on repo 333 deducted in H1 2026). Cash 20,222 is part of RMB781,951M of investment assets backing insurance liabilities, not shareholder surplus. Solvency surplus (comprehensive 237.2%, core 213.8% at 30 June 2026) is NOT added back; it is what supports the rising payout path.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 dividends declared, RMB0.68/share (interim 0.24 + final 0.44, FY2025 AR) x 22,242M shares = 15,125, a 37.5% payout of EPS 1.815. This is the observed FCFE. OCF less capex (CSV free_cash_flow 39,606 for FY2025) is premium float being invested, not free cash; the identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income is deliberately not satisfied and reported_fcf is retained for auditability only.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income (11,933 FY2025; 5,729 H1 2026) is part of the insurer's operating investment result on float and is kept in the flow, not deducted: it is not surplus-cash yield on a net-cash balance.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment, option or incentive scheme disclosed in the FY2025 Annual Report or H1 2026 interim; ShareRepurchases kpi 0 in FY2024-25 and share count unchanged since 2015. State-controlled (PICC Group 68.98%). SBC is genuinely zero, so house and street bases coincide and band_position is null.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows are RMB (CNY) millions; the HKEX H-share quote is HKD. fx_rate converts model to quote: 1 CNY = 1.1758 HKD, from Yahoo HKDCNY=X 0.8505 at 2026-10-17T21:32Z (inverted). Cross-check: 1339.HK (PICC Group) used 1.1738 from the same source on 2026-10-16T08:21Z, a 0.2% difference. 2328.HK has no A-share line, so no dual-listing parity check is available; direction is confirmed by HKD trading at a discount to CNY (HKDCNY < 1). Per-share values are computed in CNY and converted; canonical intrinsic_value / weighted_iv / entry_price are HKD, comparable to current_price. refresh_price.py moves the price but not this rate.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T08:08:14Z HKEX regular close (Friday); 52-week range 13.65-19.74. Q3 2026 results due late October 2026.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of EQUITY 9.5%, built in CNY because the flows are CNY: China 10-year government bond ~1.8% (mid-2026, approximate, same basis as 1339.HK) + beta ~1.15 x 6.5% China ERP = ~9.3%, rounded to 9.5%. Half a point BELOW the 10.0% used for parent PICC Group (1339.HK) and 1.0pt below 1336.HK / 0998.HK because PICC P&C is a pure short-tail P&C book with no guaranteed-rate life liabilities (the negative-spread risk that loaded the Group and NCI rates), core solvency 213.8%, and a 15-year record without a loss year. Not lower because total investment income is ~45-70% of profit before tax, equities and funds are ~27% of investment assets, and catastrophe/agriculture exposure is large. One rate across all three scenarios; cyclicality is carried in the bear path and its weight.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: lease liabilities RMB1,126M at FY2025 against RMB860bn of assets; the IFRS 16 charge sits inside operating expenses already deducted in profit before tax.
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial: non-controlling interests RMB2,729M of equity at FY2025 and RMB7M of FY2025 net profit (consolidated 40,377 vs attributable 40,370). No adjustment made.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE (dividends) at cost of equity on a P&C insurer, run through the component engine with net debt at zero -- the same route and mapping as parent 1339.HK (PICC Group, built 2026-10-16) and 1336.HK, for comparability (SKILL.md routing row: insurer; the routing default BVPS x exit P/B is used as a CROSS-CHECK in valuation_philosophy). Not the owner-FCF DCF: OCF of RMB20-43bn a year is premium float and EBITDA does not exist. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = insurance revenue; ebitda_margin_path = profit before tax / insurance revenue (PBT includes underwriting profit, total investment income and finance costs): FY2022 8.0%, FY2023 6.1%, FY2024 7.8%, FY2025 9.3%, H1 2025 11.6%, H2 2025 7.2%, H1 2026 15.7%; sbc = 0; da = 0 (D&A ~3.9bn is inside the expense base); cash_tax_rate 16% (ETR 14.4% FY2022, 12.4% FY2023, 15.4% FY2024, 15.4% FY2025, 19.3% H1 2026 on a higher share of taxable trading gains; tax-exempt government-bond interest and dividends keep it below 25%); capex_pct_path is the RETENTION plug = margin x (1 - tax) x (1 - payout), so FCFE = net income x payout ratio. FY2026: H1 PBT 40,029 (+38.5%) is not annualised -- H2 is seasonally weaker (catastrophe season, year-end reserving: H2 PBT 16.4bn in 2024 and 18.8bn in 2025), so the base assumes H2 2026 PBT ~17bn, FY2026 PBT ~57bn on insurance revenue +2% = 10.9% margin, NI ~47.9bn, EPS ~2.15. NORMALISATION from FY2027: underwriting at a 97% combined ratio (FY2018-25 range 97.5-99.6%, H1s 94-96%) = ~16bn, plus total investment income at ~4.8% on ~720bn of net investment assets (~35bn; total yield 5.7% FY2024, 5.8% FY2025, 3.8% unannualised H1 2026 on an A-share rally) less ~4bn finance costs and other = ~47bn PBT = 8.8% margin, ROE ~12% (FY2018-25 range ~10-14.7%, FY2025 14.7%). PAYOUT: 42% FY2019, 40% FY2020, 40.5% FY2021, 36.5% FY2022, 44.3% FY2023, 37.3% FY2024, 37.5% FY2025 (DPS 0.461/0.375/0.407/0.478/0.489/0.54/0.68). H1 2026 interim RMB0.34 (+41.7%; 23.4% of H1 EPS). Base payout 38% FY2026 -> 50% by FY2034: at a 12% ROE and ~3.5% growth the business only needs to retain ~30% of earnings, so a 50% payout still under-distributes and the FCFE value is conservative (see residual-income cross-check). Held flat at 38% the base value falls by roughly 20%.
inputs.transition_note: FY2021 and earlier revenue rows are IFRS 4 net earned premiums (344-397bn); FY2022 onward are IFRS 17 insurance revenue (FY2022 restated 424,355 in the FY2023 AR). Combined ratios and ROE are comparable enough across the break; no revenue CAGR spanning FY2021/22 is used as an input.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: insurance revenue +6.4% 3yr CAGR (IFRS 17 basis FY2022-25) but only +2.2% in H1 2026 with original premiums +1.3% and motor premiums near flat; mid-single-digit nominal P&C growth (non-motor 45% of premium, NEV insured +30.9%, technology insurance +18.5%) fading to 3% terminal. Equity CAGRs include OCI on FVOCI equities; EPS CAGRs end on a peak-yield year. None is used directly.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR (14.1%) exceeds equity 5yr CAGR (8.8%) by more than 30%: FY2020 EPS 0.938 was a trough (COVID motor-reform year, CR 98.9%) and FY2025 EPS 1.815 includes a 5.8% total investment yield and the best full-year combined ratio in the history. The 5yr revenue CAGR straddles the IFRS 4 -> 17 break. Equity is the steadier compounding gauge; the forward path is set by the ROE normalisation in inputs.notes.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are not meaningful for an insurer (OCF - capex is float); DPS is the FCFE series: 0.478 (FY2022) -> 0.68 (FY2025) = 12.5% CAGR. Net profit: 15,485 (FY2018), 24,282, 20,868, 22,360, 29,163 (FY2022), 24,585, 32,173, 40,370 (FY2025); H1 2026 32,296 (+32%). Attributable equity 141,495 (FY2018) -> 285,974 (FY2025) -> 303,688 (H1 2026) = BVPS RMB13.65.

base.narrative: FY2026: insurance revenue +2% (H1 +2.2%), H1 PBT 40.0bn plus a seasonally weak H2 of ~17bn (in line with H2 2024-25) = 10.9% margin, NI ~47.9bn (+19%), DPS ~0.82 (0.34 interim + ~0.48 final, payout 38%). FY2027: total investment yield reverts from the 2025-26 equity-rally level toward ~4.8% and the combined ratio settles at ~97% (better than the FY2018-24 average of ~98.6%, keeping part of the 'underwriting as filed' gain): margin 8.8%, NI ~39.7bn, ROE ~12%. FY2028 onward: growth 4% with non-motor, NEV and technology lines, fading to 3%; margin edges to 9.0% as the investment book grows with retained capital. Payout rises from 38% to 50% by FY2034 against 214% core solvency. Terminal min(Gordon 9.5%/3%, 16x FCFE) -- Gordon binds at ~15.8x FCFE, ~7.9x earnings, ~0.95x book at a 12% ROE.

bull.narrative: H2 2026 holds near H2 2025 plus the H1 momentum (~22bn PBT): FY2026 margin 11.8%, NI ~51.6bn. The combined ratio stays at 95-96% as motor pricing discipline, AI claims and the non-motor 'comprehensive governance' programme hold, and the total investment yield settles near 5.2% as long-term-capital equity allocations compound: margin 10.0-10.2%, ROE ~13.5%. Premium growth re-accelerates to 5% on liability, health, technology and NEV lines. Payout rises to 55% by FY2034. Terminal min(Gordon 9.5%/3.5%, 18x FCFE) -- ~1.2x book.

bear.payout_ratio_path_note: capex_pct = margin x (1 - 16.5% tax) x (1 - payout); payout 36% FY2026, 35% thereafter
bear.narrative: An H2 2026 A-share drawdown reverses fair-value gains and a catastrophe-heavy season (floods/typhoons on China's largest agricultural and catastrophe book) leaves H2 PBT ~8bn: FY2026 margin 9.2%, NI ~40bn. From FY2027 motor price competition from Ping An P&C and CPIC P&C and NEV claims inflation push the combined ratio to ~99% (FY2018-21 levels), the 10-year CGB slides toward 1.5% and the total investment yield falls to ~4%: margin 6.0%, NI ~27bn, ROE ~8% -- below the cost of equity. Growth 1-3% as motor volumes stagnate. Payout held at 35%. Terminal min(Gordon 9.5%/2.5%, 11x FCFE) -- ~0.55x book.

scenario_narratives.base: China's largest P&C insurer (33.3% share, roughly double its nearest rival) in a regulated three-player oligopoly, valued on the dividends it pays. Profit normalises from the FY2025 / H1 2026 peak (14.7% ROE, 5.8% investment yield, 94% H1 combined ratio) to a ~12% ROE built on a 97% combined ratio and a ~4.8% investment yield, grows with premiums at ~4% fading to 3%, and the payout rises from 38% toward 50% against 214% core solvency. Capitalised at a 9.5% CNY cost of equity, the shares are worth roughly 1x book -- about where they trade (0.95x H1 2026 book, ~7x FY2025 earnings, 5.3% yield).
scenario_narratives.bull: The combined ratio holds at 95-96%, investment yields stay above 5%, premium growth returns to 5% and the payout reaches 55%; ROE ~13.5% earns ~1.2x book.
scenario_narratives.bear: An equity drawdown and catastrophe season wipe out H2 2026, then motor/NEV competition and falling bond yields push the combined ratio to 99% and ROE to ~8%, below the cost of equity; the payout stays at 35% and the shares settle near 0.55x book.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%, matching parent 1339.HK: total investment income was ~68% of H1 2026 PBT and rose 58.5% on an A-share rally, so H2 2026 is exposed to markets, and catastrophe losses concentrate in H2. Not higher than 25% because the business is a pure short-tail P&C book with no guaranteed-rate life liabilities, core solvency is 214%, and it has paid a dividend and earned a profit in every year of the history. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it requires the combined ratio, the investment yield and a higher payout all to hold at once in a regulated motor market. 25/50/25 matches 1339.HK, LGEN.L and PRU.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a Chinese P&C insurer on the cash it distributes, not on OCF (premium float) and not on a peak-year net income. Profit before tax as a share of insurance revenue -- underwriting profit plus total investment income less finance costs -- is the earnings measure; after a structurally low 16% tax rate, the payout ratio (calibrated to a 36.5-44% history and the FY2025 37.5%) sets how much is retained. Debt interest is inside that measure, so net debt is zero. FY2025 and H1 2026 are peak-cycle (5.8% total investment yield, 94-97.5% combined ratio) and are normalised to a ~12% ROE. CROSS-CHECKS: (1) Book: attributable equity RMB303,688M at H1 2026 = RMB13.65/share = HKD16.05; the price is 0.95x book. A residual-income P/B at a 12% ROE, 9.5% CoE and 3% growth is (12-3)/(9.5-3) = 1.38x = HKD22, so the FCFE base, which treats retained earnings as lost cash, is the conservative of the two. (2) Earnings: FY2025 EPS RMB1.815 = HKD2.13, P/E 7.1x; normalised FY2027 EPS ~RMB1.78 = HKD2.10, P/E 7.2x. (3) Yield: FY2025 DPS RMB0.68 = HKD0.80, 5.3% yield. (4) Parent consistency: 1339.HK's sum-of-parts marks this stake at market, so a change here flows into the Group cross-check.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capital-markets leverage: total investment income 27,359 in H1 2026 (+58.5%) was ~68% of PBT; equities and funds ~27% of RMB782bn investment assets
Underwriting cycle: combined ratio 97.5% FY2025 and 94.0% H1 2026 vs 98-99.6% in FY2018-21; each 1pt of combined ratio is ~RMB5bn of PBT, ~10% of normalised profit
Motor (~44% of premium) faces regulated pricing, flat volumes and NEV claims-cost inflation; motor premium growth was 0.1-1.9%
Catastrophe and agriculture exposure as China's largest agricultural and catastrophe-scheme insurer; losses concentrate in H2
Falling China government bond yields compress the fixed-income return on ~59% of investment assets
Payout policy is a state-shareholder decision (PICC Group 68.98%); the rise from 38% to 50% is a judgment, not guidance -- held at 38% the base value falls ~20%
Q3 2026 results (late October 2026) are the first evidence on H2 2026; the base assumes H2 PBT ~17bn, the bear ~8bn
Model risk: FCFE charges retained earnings as lost; at a 12% ROE above a 9.5% CoE the residual-income cross-check is ~50% higher than the base
